hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
The affected module is the OpenTitan Entropy Source IP, specifically the shared recoverable alert output (`recov_alert`) associated with the Entropy Source `*_FIELD_ALERTS` checks. These checks detect invalid MuBi (multi-bit boolean) encodings written into MuBi-protected control fields.

## Expected Behavior
If software writes an invalid MuBi value to a protected Entropy Source control field, the corresponding `*_FIELD_ALERTS` status bit should latch and `recov_alert` should be emitted as a single alert pulse for that event. After the alert receiver completes the alert handshake, `recov_alert` should return low even if the invalid register value is still present, so one bad programmed state does not immediately retrigger additional recoverable alerts. This behavior must hold for firmware-controlled MuBi fields such as `FIPS_ENABLE`.

## Actual Behavior
`recov_alert` behaves as a level derived from the latched field-alert condition instead of as a pulse. After an invalid MuBi value is written, the alert keeps re-firing or staying asserted until software corrects the bad register value, so a single field-validation failure produces repeated recoverable alerts.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered by programming an invalid MuBi encoding into a MuBi-protected Entropy Source control field that raises a `*_FIELD_ALERTS` condition, including the `FIPS_ENABLE` case.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Emit one alert_o pulse on the rising edge of bad_field_i. Do not retrigger while the same bad condition remains high.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: A recoverable alert was driven as a level from a latched invalid-field condition, repeatedly alerting for one software error.
